title: APOLLAI, a multimodal AI system, versus EMS personnel for prehospital detection of stroke-related deficits
summary: The medRxiv abstract reports APOLLAI evaluation on video/audio recordings from 295 suspected-stroke patients at Nîmes University Hospital, against seven-neurologist consensus labels for five NIHSS items. Global sensitivity was 78.5% versus 59.4% for EMS personnel, specificity 87.0% versus 85.9%, and AUC 0.882. These are diagnostic comparisons on recorded patient data; the authors call for prospective validation in real EMS conditions.
ai_technology: APOLLAI (computer vision, audio deep learning and SVM fusion classifier)

evidence.tested: Recorded cases from 295 suspected-stroke patients; AI and EMS assessments compared with consensus labels for five neurological tasks.
evidence.unknown: Complete abstract and original-server metadata reviewed; full methods, model-selection timing and external EMS generalizability were not assessed. Authors explicitly call for real-world prospective validation.
evidence.ai_role: A multimodal machine-learning system detected stroke-related neurological deficits from video and audio recordings and was compared with clinicians' assessments.
